title: At, in and on: prepositions of time
summary: Предлоги времени **at / on / in**, их тонкие случаи (**at night, on Friday morning, in the night**), пары **on time / in time**, **at the end / in the end** и случаи без предлога.
ru:
## Основная схема: at, on, in
Базовое правило вы знаете: **at** — точка во времени, **on** — день и дата, **in** — более длинный отрезок. На уровне Advanced важны детали и пары, которые путают даже уверенные ученики.
> at 7.30 · at noon · at midnight · at the end of the week — в 7:30, в полдень, в полночь, в конце недели
> on Tuesday · on 3 May · on Christmas Day · on my birthday — во вторник, 3 мая, в Рождество, в мой день рождения
> in June · in 2018 · in the summer · in the 1990s · in the twenty-first century — в июне, в 2018, летом, в 90-е, в XXI веке

## Части суток и дни: где меняется предлог
- **in the morning / afternoon / evening**, но **at night**: *I work best in the morning, but I sleep badly at night.*
- Если часть суток привязана к дню или дате, предлог меняется на **on**: *on Friday morning*, *on the evening of 12 June*, *on a cold winter's night*.
- **in the night** означает «ночью» в конкретный раз, обычно что-то случилось: *I woke up in the night and heard a noise.* А **at night** — обычно, вообще.
- **at the weekend** (британский вариант) = **on the weekend** (американский): *We go hiking at the weekend / on weekends.*
- Праздничный период — **at Christmas / at Easter** (вся пора), а конкретный день — **on Christmas Day / on Easter Sunday**.

## Через сколько: in и within
**in** + срок указывает на момент в будущем, отсчитанный от сейчас: *The results will be ready in ten days.* — через десять дней. Часто добавляют *in two weeks' time*. А **within** + срок — «не позже чем за / в пределах»: *You must reply within ten days.* Нельзя путать с **for ten days** («в течение десяти дней» — длительность, см. юнит 93).

## Пары, которые различают по смыслу
| | |
|---|---|
| **on time** — точно в срок, не опоздав | The flight left **on time**. |
| **in time** — достаточно рано, чтобы успеть | We arrived **in time** to see the start. |
| **at the end (of)** — в самом конце чего-то | **At the end of** the film, everyone clapped. |
| **in the end** — в итоге, в конце концов | **In the end**, she accepted the offer. |
| **at first** — сначала (потом иначе) | **At first** I hated it; now I love it. |
| **at the beginning / in the beginning** — в начале | **At the beginning of** the lecture... |

## Без предлога
Предлог не нужен перед **this, last, next, every, each, some, any, all, one**: *next Friday*, *last summer*, *every morning*, *this evening*. А также в вопросах типа *What time...?* и в разговорных формах: *I'll see you Monday.* (американский вариант, без on).
- ~~I'll call you on next Monday.~~ → I'll call you **next Monday.**
- ~~We met in last June.~~ → We met **last June.**

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~The meeting is in Monday.~~ → The meeting is **on** Monday.
- ~~She was born at 1990.~~ → She was born **in** 1990.
- ~~I'll be back at ten minutes.~~ → I'll be back **in** ten minutes.
- ~~In the end of the book, he dies.~~ → **At** the end of the book, he dies.
- ~~I don't like driving in night.~~ → I don't like driving **at night**. (без артикля — только at night)
en:
## The basic pattern: at, on, in
You know the basic idea: **at** is a point in time, **on** is a day or date, and **in** is a longer period. At Advanced level the details matter, and so do a few pairs that confuse even confident learners.
> at 7.30 · at noon · at midnight · at the end of the week
> on Tuesday · on 3 May · on Christmas Day · on my birthday
> in June · in 2018 · in the summer · in the 1990s · in the twenty-first century

## Parts of the day: where the preposition changes
- **in the morning / afternoon / evening**, but **at night**: *I work best in the morning, but I sleep badly at night.*
- When a part of the day belongs to a particular day or date, we use **on**: *on Friday morning*, *on the evening of 12 June*, *on a cold winter's night*.
- **in the night** refers to one particular night, usually when something happened: *I woke up in the night and heard a noise.* **at night** is general or habitual.
- **at the weekend** (British) = **on the weekend** (American): *We go hiking at the weekend / on weekends.*
- A holiday period is **at Christmas / at Easter** (the whole season), a specific day is **on Christmas Day / on Easter Sunday**.

## How long from now: in and within
**in** + a period gives the moment in the future that is counted from now: *The results will be ready in ten days.* We often say *in two weeks' time*. **within** + a period means "no later than" or "inside that limit": *You must reply within ten days.* Do not confuse it with **for ten days**, which shows duration (see Unit 93).

## Pairs that differ in meaning
| | |
|---|---|
| **on time** — punctual, not late | The flight left **on time**. |
| **in time** — early enough to do something | We arrived **in time** to see the start. |
| **at the end (of)** — at the very last point | **At the end of** the film, everyone clapped. |
| **in the end** — finally, after everything | **In the end**, she accepted the offer. |
| **at first** — originally (things changed later) | **At first** I hated it; now I love it. |
| **at the beginning / in the beginning** — at the start | **At the beginning of** the lecture... |

## No preposition
We use no preposition before **this, last, next, every, each, some, any, all, one**: *next Friday*, *last summer*, *every morning*, *this evening*. In informal American English we can also drop on before days: *I'll see you Monday.*
- ~~I'll call you on next Monday.~~ → I'll call you **next Monday.**
- ~~We met in last June.~~ → We met **last June.**

## Common mistakes
- ~~The meeting is in Monday.~~ → The meeting is **on** Monday.
- ~~She was born at 1990.~~ → She was born **in** 1990.
- ~~I'll be back at ten minutes.~~ → I'll be back **in** ten minutes.
- ~~In the end of the book, he dies.~~ → **At** the end of the book, he dies.
- ~~I don't like driving in night.~~ → I don't like driving **at night**. (without an article it is always at night)
structure:
## Формула выбора
| Предлог | Что выражает | Примеры |
|---|---|---|
| at | точное время, момент, праздничный период, ночь | at 6.15 · at noon · at night · at Christmas · at the weekend (BrE) |
| on | дни, даты, конкретный день + часть суток | on Friday · on 5 May · on Monday morning · on New Year's Eve |
| in | месяцы, годы, сезоны, века, части суток, срок «через» | in July · in 2024 · in the 1980s · in the evening · in ten minutes |
| (нет) | this, last, next, every, each, some, all | next week · every day · last spring |

## Пары по смыслу
> **on time** (вовремя) ≠ **in time** (успеть)
> **at the end of** + что именно ≠ **in the end** (итог, без of)
> **in** + срок = через · **within** + срок = не позже чем через

## Британский и американский варианты
| BrE | AmE |
|---|---|
| at the weekend | on the weekend |
| at weekends | on weekends |
| Monday to Friday | Monday through Friday |

items.text: My sister was born {{in}} the spring of 1994, and I was born {{on}} 3 April 1991.
Many companies close {{at}} Christmas and reopen {{in}} January.
The first successful experiment took place {{in}} the 1960s.
I'll see you {{on}} the morning of 14 May.
The report will be ready {{in}} ten days.
We usually go to the mountains {{at|on}} the weekend.

exercises.title: in time или on time? at the end или in the end?
exercises.instruction: Вставьте нужное выражение. В скобках — пара, из которой нужно выбрать.

items.text: The train was punctual, so we arrived {{on}} time.
We got to the station just {{in}} time to catch the last train.
They argued for hours, but {{in the end}} they signed the contract.
items.hint: at the end / in the end

items.text: There is a short quiz {{at the end}} of each chapter.
items.hint: at the end / in the end

items.text: {{At first}} I didn't like the city, but now I love it.
The film is set {{in}} the early nineteenth century.
{{At}} the moment, the manager is in a meeting.
Can you reply {{within}} two days? We can't wait longer.

items.why: Перед **next, last, this, every** предлог не нужен.

items.q: She was born ___ the morning of 3 April.
items.why: Часть суток конкретной даты — **on the morning of**.

items.q: I always get up early ___ weekdays.
items.why: Дни недели (во множественном числе тоже) — **on weekdays**.

items.q: He started the company ___ the age of 25.
I'm usually busy ___ the morning, but free after lunch.
The deadline is ___ the end of the month.
The phone rang ___ the middle of the night.
items.why: **in the middle of the night** — устойчивое выражение.

options: I'll call you on next Monday.
I'll call you in next Monday.
The play starts at half past seven on Saturday evening.
The play starts in half past seven at Saturday evening.
The play starts on half past seven in Saturday evening.
items.why: Время — **at**, день с частью суток — **on Saturday evening**.

options: Don't worry, the film begins in ten minutes.
Don't worry, the film begins on ten minutes.
Don't worry, the film begins at ten minutes.
We visit my parents at Christmas Day.
We visit my parents on Christmas Day.
We visit my parents in Christmas Day.
items.why: Конкретный день — **on Christmas Day** (но *at Christmas* — праздничная пора).

options: I woke up at the night and heard a noise.
I woke up in the night and heard a noise.
I woke up on night and heard a noise.
items.why: Один конкретный случай — **in the night**; ~~at the night~~ и ~~on night~~ невозможны (без артикля — *at night*).

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте на вопросы полными предложениями, следя за предлогами времени.

items.prompt: What time do you usually get up on weekdays?
items.sample: I usually get up at 6.30 on weekdays.

items.prompt: What do you do at the weekend (or on the weekend)?
items.sample: At the weekend I usually visit my parents.

items.prompt: When were you born? Give the full date.
What are you going to do in the next few weeks?

items.prompt: Describe a time when you arrived in time (or too late) for something important.
items.sample: Last year I got to the airport just in time to catch my flight.
